# `Q-10-3` — Partial Not Found

> A template's `$partial(name)$` reference names a partial file
> that does not exist.

## What this means

Pandoc-flavored templates can compose smaller fragments
(partials) through `$partial("name.tex")$` or
`$partial("name.html")$`. The partial is looked up at compile
time. This error fires when no partial with the requested name
can be found on the template search path.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo in the partial filename.**
- **The partial lives in a directory** that the template
  engine is not searching. Partials are resolved relative to
  the calling template's directory and any directories the
  build adds to the search path.
- **A partial that was renamed or deleted** without updating
  its references.

## How to fix

Confirm the partial file exists at the path the engine is
looking for. The simplest verification is to put the file
beside the calling template — if the reference resolves then,
the previous location was off the search path.

## Related

- `Q-10-5` — unresolved partial reference: similar shape, but
  the reference made it into the parsed template without being
  resolved at compile time (a different code path).
- `Q-10-4` — recursive partial: the partial exists but
  ultimately includes itself.
